road.name: Eagle Peak Trailhead, Longmire, Mount Rainier NP (Tatoosh Range access)
road.status: Paved park road to Longmire year-round (weather permitting).
road.driveNote: From the Nisqually (SW) entrance, drive via Longmire and Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction, then east about 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes pullouts; the Pinnacle Peak/Castle trailhead is on the south side of the road, directly across from the lakes. In winter, park instead at the year-round Narada Falls lot and approach on skis/snowshoes.
road.seasonalGate: Gated and closed by snow roughly mid-October through late May/early June, depending on snowpack; also subject to intermittent summer closures for road-rehab construction — check NPS road status before driving.

waypoints.name: Pinnacle Peak Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
waypoints.note: Shared trailhead for Pinnacle Peak, Plummer Peak, and The Castle; hike 2 miles up Pinnacle Peak Trail then contour south/east across scree below Pinnacle's summit to reach The Castle's SE side.

before.rappels: One ~40 ft rappel off fixed slings on the summit block; downclimbing the easy 5th-class line is also common.
before.descent: Downclimb the easy 5th-class line, or make a single short (~40 ft) rappel from the fixed slings on the summit block, then reverse the chimney pitch from the notch.

hazards: Exposed terrain at saddle with fall consequences
Loose rock holds on Class 4 bypass section
Avalanche danger on steep meadow in winter (requires avalanche skills)

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late spring (May-June) on lingering snow is best for efficient climbing and glissade descent; the route remains open and permitted through October but is loose and tedious once snow-free

May.reason: Residual snow cover often still present early in the month, allowing efficient glissade descent; permit demand is lower under the larger Apr1-May14 quota

July.reason: Typically snow-free — route becomes loose volcanic ash and boulders; hot and exposed

June.reason: Prime snow-climbing/glissade conditions; high weekend demand under the tighter 110/day quota

August.reason: Driest, hottest month; heat and lack of water called out as a specific hazard

October.reason: Early snow and storms can return; permit quota season ends Oct 31, after which the route effectively transitions toward Worm Flows winter conditions

September.reason: Cooler temperatures than midsummer, still dry/loose underfoot, generally stable weather

access.fees: A Washington Sno-Park permit (or Forest Service equivalent) is required to park at Marble Mountain Sno-Park during the winter Sno-Park season.
access.notes: Daily quota: 350 climbers/day (Apr 1–May 14), 110 climbers/day (May 15–Oct 31). This is a distinct fee/permit system from both Mount Rainier’s $82 Climbing Cost Recovery Fee and Mount Adams’ $20 Climbing Pass — do not conflate them.
access.rules: Group size capped at 12. Stay at least 30 ft back from the crater rim — cornices are unstable and have caused fatalities; entry into the crater is strictly prohibited. Blue bags required for human waste above treeline.
access.permit: November 1-March 31: climbing permits are free and self-issued at the Marble Mountain Sno-Park kiosk. April 1-October 31: permits are limited and must be purchased in advance on Recreation.gov (released one month at a time), since the quota season applies mountain-wide regardless of which trailhead is used.
access.closures: Crater entry is prohibited year-round; stay back from the cornice-prone rim edge.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service — Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument.
access.land_manager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)
access.parking_pass: $5/day/vehicle at Climber’s Bivouac, waived with a valid climbing permit.

overnight_permit.what: Mount St. Helens climbing permit for travel above 4,800 ft; no permit to camp at the roadhead
overnight_permit.where: April 1 to October 31 buy it in advance on Recreation.gov (daily quota, fee per climber). November 1 to March 31 it is free and self-issued at the trailhead kiosk. Camping above 4,800 ft is not allowed.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous full-day climb, roughly 8-9 miles round trip with about 4,500 ft of gain on snow, potentially with postholing in soft/unconsolidated conditions
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate winter mountaineering kit (ice axe, crampons, extra insulation/layers, navigation tools; avalanche gear recommended for higher-risk periods)

partner_requirements.approachTime: No separate approach — climb begins at Marble Mountain Sno-Park trailhead; typically a 7-10 hour round trip
requiredSkills: Ice axe self-arrest and crampon technique on sustained steep snow
Cornice awareness near the crater rim, where fatalities from cornice collapse are a noted hazard
Basic avalanche hazard evaluation for wind-loaded slopes and storm-loading conditions
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate-to-advanced winter mountaineering experience required — this is a non-technical grade but a serious winter snow climb, not a beginner outing

itinerary.cal: Standard winter/spring route Dec-May when snow covers the volcanic rubble; requires a WA Sno-Park permit Dec 1-Mar 31 in addition to the climbing permit.

days.note: Worm Flows is climbed as a single long day from Marble Mountain Sno-Park, not backpacked - no established high camp. The route climbs through forest, crosses Swift Creek above Chocolate Falls, then follows a long open ridge of packed snow/lava rubble to the crater rim; most parties glissade much of the descent.
days.title: Car-to-car summit day

schedule.label: Leave Marble Mountain Sno-Park
schedule.detail: Early start typical; Washington Sno-Park permit required Dec 1-Mar 31, plus climbing permit.

schedule.label: Cross Swift Creek above Chocolate Falls
schedule.detail: ~2 miles in, exit forest around 3,750 ft near the falls.

schedule.label: Gain the ridge / treeline
schedule.detail: Open snow slopes begin; rope up or don crampons as conditions dictate.

schedule.label: Reach crater rim
schedule.detail: Trip reports commonly show rim arrival around 12:45 PM on a dawn start; summit ~8,363 ft.

schedule.label: Summit break
schedule.detail: Rest, food, views before the long glissade descent.

schedule.label: Glissade/descend to sno-park
schedule.detail: Snow slopes make for a fast glissade descent back to the trailhead.

days.objective: Reach the crater rim via Worm Flows and return to Marble Mountain Sno-Park

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day: about 9-10 hrs car-to-car, 5,700 ft gain over roughly 12 miles round trip, no camp required.
